## Data and Access Risk

- **Legal compulsion makes "no access" assurances meaningless.** PRC law — National Intelligence Law Article 7 ("all organizations and citizens shall support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts"), the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, and the amended Counter-Espionage Law — imposes affirmative cooperation duties on PRC companies and their personnel ([China Law Translate](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/); [Lawfare](https://www.lawfaremedia.org/article/beijings-new-national-intelligence-law-defense-offense)). Any representation by Z.ai that customer content is not retained or shared is a commercial statement, not a legal constraint, and it is unverifiable from outside.
- **The Singapore front does not change the threat model.** Z.ai's international API is controlled by Jingsheng Hengxing Technology Pte. Ltd. (Singapore), with a DPA asserting real-time processing and no server-side storage of API content; third-party reviews find no retention table, abuse-review exception disclosure, or third-party audit behind the claim ([Z.ai Privacy Policy](https://docs.z.ai/legal-agreement/privacy-policy); [Standard Compute](https://standardcompute.com/providers/z-ai); [Erkin Ekici, LLM API privacy comparison](https://erkinekici.com/articles/comparing-llm-api-privacy/)). The mainland endpoint (open.bigmodel.cn) hosts in China. The collected data set is broad: account identifiers, device and network information, usage and browsing history, log files, and "user content" including prompts; the policy reserves use of data for model training and collection of public information "to train our models" ([Z.ai Privacy Policy](https://docs.z.ai/legal-agreement/privacy-policy)).
- **What US users are actually sending.** The dominant use case is code: the GLM Coding Plan plugs GLM into Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, and 20+ agentic harnesses ([Z.ai docs](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/overview)) and went viral in North American developer communities at $3/month before prices doubled ([Remio](https://www.remio.ai/post/the-glm-coding-plan-went-viral-in-north-america-then-the-price-doubled)). Internal telemetry shows ~2,300 US-origin organizations on Z.ai endpoints; SBOM sampling shows GLM in US customer-support bots and document-processing products — categories that ingest customer PII, HR data, and business-sensitive text. Six federal contractors are among the integrating products, meaning prompts may plausibly include CUI or government-related data.
- **DOJ Data Security Program hook.** Zhipu is a "covered person" under 28 CFR part 202 because entities on the BIS Entity List are within the covered-person classes ([DOJ DSP Compliance Guide](https://www.justice.gov/opa/media/1396356/dl); [28 CFR 202.211](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-28/chapter-I/part-202/subpart-B/section-202.211)). Covered data transactions — vendor agreements, employment agreements, investment agreements, and data brokerage — that give Zhipu access to government-related data or bulk US sensitive personal data are prohibited or restricted (restricted transactions require CISA security requirements) ([28 CFR 202.401](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-28/chapter-I/part-202/subpart-D); [DOJ NSD Data Security](https://www.justice.gov/nsd/data-security)). US persons' use of the Z.ai API under a paid vendor agreement that exposes government-related or bulk sensitive personal data may already be unlawful absent compliance measures — an enforcement and outreach priority regardless of what OICTS decides on ICTS grounds.
- **Demonstrated party-state control of the service.** GLM served from Z.ai's own endpoint returns blank completions — not refusals — on Tiananmen 1989 and Falun Gong questions; the pattern is stable across GLM releases 4.5 through 5.2 and is applied at Z.ai's serving layer (the same weights answer freely when served by neutral hosts) ([FreedomBench/TrustedRouter](https://trustedrouter.com/blog/the-ai-models-that-go-silent-on-china); [SpeechMap, GLM-4.6](https://speechmap.ai/models/z-ai-glm-4-6/)). This is direct, observable evidence that Zhipu operates content controls aligned to PRC state security preferences on its commercial service.
- **Adjacent collection: AMiner.** Zhipu owns and operates AMiner, a research-intelligence platform profiling millions of researchers worldwide, including US government and defense-adjacent scientists ([Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)). Aggregated S&T-workforce data of this kind is a classic counterintelligence input and should be treated as a standing collection capability of the parent company.

**Assessment:** We assess with high confidence that the hosted-API channel presents the most acute data risk in this case: US-origin source code, documents, and personal data are flowing at scale into infrastructure ultimately controlled by an Entity-Listed PRC company that is legally obligated to assist PRC security services and demonstrably applies party-state content rules to its service.

## Open-Weight Distribution Risk

- **Irreversibility and proliferation.** GLM-4.5 and later releases ship under MIT/Apache-2.0 terms with free commercial use ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai); [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5)); zai-org repositories exceed 9M cumulative downloads (internal count; GLM-5 alone shows ~2.2M all-time downloads on Hugging Face, with US inference providers Novita, Featherless, and DeepInfra serving it, [HF model page](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5)). Weights cannot be recalled, patched centrally, or version-controlled downstream; mirrors and derivatives persist indefinitely.
- **Unverifiable trust.** CISA's input is the correct technical baseline: no malicious behavior observed in GLM weights to date, but backdoors and poisoning "are hard to rule out" (case file). The research record supports that caution: Anthropic demonstrated deceptive behaviors that survive safety training and elude red-teaming; 2026 research demonstrates latent malice implantable in tool-using open-weight agents via parameter-efficient fine-tuning with minimal capability signature ([Anthropic Sleeper Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/sleeper-agents-training-deceptive-llms-that-persist-through-safety-training); [arXiv 2603.03371](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.03371v1)). A 744B-parameter model cannot be audited exhaustively; "the community reviewed it" is not a security control.
- **Agentic deployment multiplies blast radius.** GLM is marketed for long-horizon agentic coding (GLM-5's stated focus is "complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks"; 200K→1M-token contexts in GLM-5.2) ([Z.ai blog, GLM-5](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5); [Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html)) and ships in harnesses (ZCode; Claude Code/Cline/Cursor integrations) with filesystem and shell access ([Z.ai docs](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/overview)). A subverted or subtly biased model in an agentic role can exfiltrate repositories, insert exploitable code, or bias automated decisions — the highest-impact scenario in this case.
- **Standards and ecosystem capture.** Widespread GLM adoption imports PRC technical choices (tokenizers, chat templates, evals, guardrail patterns) into US tooling and normalizes a PRC vendor across the developer base; the state fund's explicit linkage of investment to open-source capability building shows this is strategy, not philanthropy ([NSTI](https://www.ncsti.gov.cn/kjdt/xwjj/202504/t20250418_202045.html)). Chinese-built models reached 61% of OpenRouter token share by February 2026 ([Dataconomy](https://dataconomy.com/2026/02/25/chinese-ai-models-hit-61-market-share-on-openrouter/)).
- **DoD networks (responding to DoD's input).** Open weights downloaded by individual developers or contractors are the hardest channel to police on DoD networks: no procurement record exists; SBOM/AI-BOM disclosure is currently voluntary and inconsistent. A DoD network prohibition without a contractor flow-down and AI-BOM attestation requirement would leave the dominant entry path (contractor toolchains) open.
- **What the evidence does and does not show.** Third-party testing indicates the Tiananmen/Falun Gong refusals are enforced at Z.ai's serving endpoint rather than in the released weights (the same GLM versions answer freely on neutral hosts) ([TrustedRouter](https://trustedrouter.com/blog/the-ai-models-that-go-silent-on-china)). That nuance matters for calibrating measures — it means self-hosted weights are not currently a censorship vector — but it does not reduce the backdoor/trust problem, which no test can resolve, and it confirms Z.ai's endpoint is an instrument of party-state content control.

**Assessment:** We assess with moderate confidence that the open-weight channel is the strategically most dangerous vector in this case — not because malice has been demonstrated (it has not), but because the channel is unrecallable, unauditable, state-subsidized, and now embedded in 41 US products including federal contractor toolchains, while the USG currently has no visibility or control instrument over it.

## US Exposure

*Internal OICTS data-team estimates as of 6 October 2026 (CUI//PROPIN):*

- **Hosted API:** ~2,300 US-origin organizations observed calling Z.ai/bigmodel.cn endpoints in Q3 2026 (cooperating-provider CDN telemetry; low precision, sectoral breakdown unavailable).
- **Open weights:** GLM-4.x/5.x mirrored on Hugging Face (zai-org); available through ≥9 US cloud marketplaces and inference providers (OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, Baseten; Hugging Face lists Novita, Featherless, DeepInfra, and zai-org's own inference endpoint as providers, [HF GLM-5](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5)).
- **Enterprise integration:** GLM identified in 41 US software products via SBOM sampling (coding assistants, customer-support bots, document processing); 6 are federal contractors.
- **Downloads:** >9M cumulative across zai-org repositories (all geographies).
- **Corroborating open-source indicators of scale:** GLM 5.3 Flash ranked #3 globally on OpenRouter with 12.9T tokens processed in the week through 15 Oct 2026 ([OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/rankings)); GLM 5.2 was the top open-weight model on the Artificial Analysis index in June 2026 ([OpenRouter blog](https://openrouter.ai/blog/insights/the-open-weight-models-that-matter-june-2026/)); ZCode reached 1M users ([Runtimewire](https://runtimewire.com/article/zai-zcode-one-million-users-long-running-coding-agents)); the $3 GLM Coding Plan spread through North American developer communities before pricing doubled in April 2026 ([Remio](https://www.remio.ai/post/the-glm-coding-plan-went-viral-in-north-america-then-the-price-doubled); [Rivestack/HN](https://ask.rivestack.io/story/zai-doubles-its-coding-plan-prices-47756002)).
- **Financial exposure:** US persons may hold HKEX-listed shares (2513), and US institutions can hold exposure through the forthcoming STAR Market listing; Treasury/OIA input on the scale of US holdings is outstanding (case file). Zhipu's direct US commercial revenue is negligible (~US$123K on-premise, 9M 2025 — [ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/zhipu-and-minimax-ipo)), underscoring that US entanglement is ecosystem-based rather than contract-based.

**Assessment:** US exposure is material, growing, and concentrated exactly where harm potential is greatest: developer toolchains (code access), support automation (PII ingestion), and — through six federal contractors — the federal enterprise. If unaddressed, adoption compounding (each integration creates a constituency and a switching cost) will make future restriction progressively harder. Every quarter of delay purchases permanent dependence.

## Mitigation Options / Recommended Measures

Options are arrayed from least to most restrictive. Recommended package: **A + B + C + D now**, with E prepared as contingency escalation. Full one-paragraph treatments with trade-offs are in `measures.md` (M1–M9).

| Option | Description | Enforceability | Principal trade-offs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Monitoring + guidance** (M1, M2) | Sustain telemetry/SBOM collection; CISA guidance to federal agencies and critical infrastructure on GLM risks; request ODNI classified annex | High | Lowest cost, but does not alter adoption trajectory; guidance alone is what CISA already deems the minimum |
| **B. Federal-sector removal + procurement flow-downs** (M2, M3) | Prohibit GLM ICTS on federal and DoD networks; FAR/DFARS clause barring GLM in contractor systems processing CUI or government data; AI-BOM/SBOM attestation; GSA/DoD cloud catalog scrub | High (procurement is the strongest lever the USG has) | Modest industry friction; research use inside agencies requires a licensed carve-out |
| **C. ICTS Initial Determination — hosted API** (M4) | Prohibit US persons' use of Z.ai/bigmodel.cn endpoints where transactions involve government-related data, bulk US sensitive personal data, critical-infrastructure operations, or DIB activity; enforcement via payment, CDN, app-store, and US cloud on-ramps; DOJ DSP alignment | High for institutional users; moderate for individuals (VPN residual) | Novel application of Part 791 to LLM services; retaliation risk; litigation risk manageable (service transaction, not code) |
| **D. ICTS channel conditions — open weights** (M5) | Mitigation order/conditions on US-based hubs and marketplaces: risk labeling, provenance/attestation, exclusion from federal-use catalogs and FedRAMP/DoD marketplace offerings; general distribution continues with disclosure pending review | High (hubs/marketplaces are US companies subject to US orders) | Does not reach already-downloaded copies; research community friction; avoids the code-as-speech exposure of a blanket code ban |
| **E. Full class prohibition via rulemaking** (M6, M7) | Connected-vehicles-style rule prohibiting all US transactions involving GLM-family ICTS (API, marketplace distribution, integration) with a licensed research/evaluation exception; Entity List/affiliates maintenance | Moderate — enforceable at institutional/channel level, not at self-hosting margin | Highest deterrence and clearest signal; but novel, hard to enforce against self-hosted weights, invites PRC retaliation against US firms, and fragmentation of US AI tooling; reserve for escalation triggers |

**Enforceability analysis (responding to State/EB).** State is right that banning private possession of open weights would be novel and, at the margin, unenforceable — and wrong that this counsels against restrictive action. {"path": "/workspace/out/measures.md", "content": "# ICTS Case 2026-0412 — Recommended Measures
**Subject: Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai / Knowledge Atlas Technology, HKEX: 2513) — GLM-family models**

CUI//PROPIN

Prepared by: OICTS Analytic Cell, 16 October 2026 — companion to `assessment.md`. The Executive Director requested a range from monitoring through prohibition with the trade-offs of each; measures are ordered by escalating restrictiveness and each is stated in a single paragraph. **Recommended immediate package: M1–M5.** M6–M9 are contingency and cross-cutting actions. Analysts recommend; the Executive Director and Under Secretary decide.

---

**M1 — Intensified monitoring and intelligence development (baseline; do regardless of what else is chosen).** Stand up a standing OICTS/BIS/CISA collection cell that maintains the SBOM/AI-BOM sampling program that identified GLM in 41 US products, refreshes the cooperating-provider CDN telemetry quarterly to track the ~2,300 US-origin organizations calling Z.ai endpoints, and watches the nine-plus US inference marketplaces for GLM token-share growth (OpenRouter already shows GLM 5.3 Flash at #3 with 12.9T weekly tokens); formally request the ODNI classified annex, task Treasury/OIA for holdings and payment-flow data, and direct BIS to confirm in primary sources the current Entity List status of all ten Zhipu-family entities in light of third-party tracker records showing two affiliates delisted on 28 July 2026. Trade-offs: essentially no economic cost and no retaliation surface, but monitoring alone does not change the adoption trajectory — every quarter without action compounds US integration — and it buys information only if collection is actually resourced.

**M2 — CISA/DHS guidance and a federal-sector removal directive.** At minimum, CISA should immediately issue guidance (binding operational direction for FCEB agencies, advisory for critical infrastructure) that GLM-family models and Z.ai endpoints are foreign-adversary ICTS from an Entity-Listed supplier, are prohibited on federal information systems, and present specific risks: presumptive PRC legal access to prompts and outputs, endpoint-level censorship demonstrating party-state control of the service, and unverifiable trust in agentic coding contexts; DHS should extend the advisory to state/local/tribal/territorial governments and the critical infrastructure sectors it covers, with a reporting channel for discovered integrations. This answers CISA's own recommendation ("guidance for federal agencies at minimum") and DoD's request that the product address open weights on DoD networks: DoD should issue a matching USCYBERCOM/DoD CIO direction for DoD networks and the DJWCC cloud catalogs. Trade-offs: high enforceability inside government, no direct cost to the private economy, and it establishes the record for escalation; but it leaves the six federal contractors' own systems and the broader private sector untouched, and guidance without a procurement hook (M3) will be inconsistently implemented inside the sprawling federal enterprise.

**M3 — Federal procurement and contractor flow-downs (the strongest lever the USG has).** Publish a FAR/DFARS clause prohibiting federal contractors from using GLM-family models, Z.ai endpoints, or derivative GLM-based services in any system that processes CUI, government-related data, or deliverables under federal contracts, paired with a mandatory AI-BOM/SBOM disclosure and attestation requirement so that GLM embedded in a vendor's toolchain (coding assistants, support bots, document processing) is visible to contracting officers; scrub GSA schedules and DoD cloud marketplaces of any offering serving GLM; and require the six identified federal contractors to certify remediation. Trade-offs: enforceable through contract law and suspension/debarment, reaches the highest-risk exposure (federal enterprise and DIB) without regulating the economy at large, and creates the audit trail nothing else currently provides; the costs are compliance friction for contractors who must find substitutes (real but bounded — US and allied alternatives exist in every category GLM appears in), some detection burden on agencies, and the need for a narrow licensed exception so federal researchers can still evaluate adversarial models — which is a national-security requirement, not a courtesy.

**M4 — ICTS Initial Determination prohibiting Z.ai hosted-API use in national-security-sensitive contexts.** Issue an Initial Determination under 15 CFR part 791 finding that the acquisition, use, or dealing in Z.ai's hosted API services (api.z.ai, open.bigmodel.cn) by US persons poses an undue and unacceptable risk where the transaction involves government-related data, bulk US sensitive personal data, critical-infrastructure operations, or defense-industrial-base activity, and direct cessation of those uses; enforce through the service's US chokepoints — payment processors, app stores, US CDN and cloud on-ramps — and align enforcement with the DOJ Data Security Program, under which Zhipu is already a "covered person" by virtue of its Entity List status (restricted transactions require CISA security requirements; data brokerage involving bulk sensitive data is prohibited outright). This measure treats the hosted API for what it is: a channel moving US code, documents, and personal data into infrastructure controlled by an Entity-Listed PRC company that is legally compelled to assist PRC intelligence and demonstrably applies party-state content controls. Trade-offs: novel application of Part 791 to an LLM API invites litigation, but it is materially better positioned than a code ban because it regulates a commercial service transaction, not speech; institutional compliance is enforceable while individual VPN circumvention is a residual; PRC retaliation against US firms in China is likely but asymmetric — the PRC already blocks US AI services, and the market Zhipu would lose (US enterprise) is precisely the market whose loss is the point; and a blanket consumer ban would be over-inclusive, hence the sensitive-context scoping.

**M5 — Channel conditions on open-weight distribution through US hubs and marketplaces.** Rather than an unenforceable ban on possession, use the Initial Determination to impose enforceable conditions on the US-based distribution channels: Hugging Face (zai-org repositories) and US inference marketplaces (Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, Baseten, OpenRouter-listed providers) must carry prominent foreign-adversary provenance and risk labeling, attest that they do not return customer prompts, telemetry, or fine-tune feedback to Z.ai or its fronts, exclude GLM models from any federal-use catalog, FedRAMP or DoD marketplace offering, or co-marketing with government offerings, and maintain takedown/notice capability for future GLM releases pending case-by-case review. General consumer and developer distribution continues under disclosure pending the interagency's decision on a broader rule. Trade-offs: this reaches every future download at the point of distribution (the only point the USG can reach) without attempting the impossible recall of 9M+ existing downloads; it preserves US research access to a leading open-weight family, which has genuine defensive value (red-teaming, counter-model development, standards work) and avoids the First Amendment code-as-speech exposure that a publication ban would invite; the costs are friction for the hubs (US companies, subject to US jurisdiction — enforceable), a likely PRC propaganda windfall ("US bans open source"), and the admission that self-hosted copies already on US machines are out of reach — which is why the measure pairs with disclosure and liability rules rather than pretending a ban would work there.

**M6 — Full class prohibition via rulemaking (contingency; recommend preparing, not issuing, now).** If the interagency concludes that presence-based restriction is insufficient — triggers would include evidence of PRC intelligence tasking of Zhipu, discovery of malicious functionality in GLM weights, GLM penetration of US critical-infrastructure control chains, or continued growth of embedded integration after M3–M5 — OICTS should move a connected-vehicles-style rulemaking under Part 791 prohibiting all US transactions involving GLM-family ICTS: hosted API, marketplace distribution, enterprise integration, and new weight releases, with a narrow licensed exception for evaluation, security research, and countermeasure development. The January 2025 connected-vehicles rule is the template for exactly this kind of class-based prohibition and survived its comment process; a rule makes compliance obligations clear, uniform, and private-sector-enforceable rather than case-by-case orders. Trade-offs: maximum deterrence and clarity, but it is the most aggressive option — a self-hosted-weights ban is novel and weakly enforceable at the margin (State's enforceability concern is correct), litigation risk on open-weight distribution is real, retaliation against US hardware and consumer firms in China is probable, and it would fragment US AI tooling that has come to depend on the best available open models; those costs are defensible only if the risk record matures to match them, which is why this cell recommends preparation and triggers rather than immediate issuance.

**M7 — Entity List and trade-control maintenance.** Direct BIS to verify the status of all ten Zhipu-family entries against primary sources (given the unresolved 28 July 2026 affiliate-delist records), to treat the 9 November 2026 automatic reimposition of the suspended Affiliates Rule as the mechanism that captures new Zhipu subsidiaries, the renamed Knowledge Atlas entity, and any future fronts (including the Singapore vehicle Jingsheng Hengxing if ownership tracing supports it), and to consider additional listings for any Zhipu-affiliated distribution or services entities identified through M1 telemetry. Where export licensing still matters (US cloud and chip flows that indirectly touch Zhipu's foreign deployments), apply end-use certification. Trade-offs: low-cost, well-understood instruments with interagency precedent — but in the current truce environment, additions are politically constrained (the administration has reportedly withheld DeepSeek/CXMT listings), Entity List actions no longer bite on Zhipu itself since it now trains on domestic silicon, and the truce itself is a fragile framework that could reimpose the Affiliates Rule or drop it again; M7 is necessary housekeeping, not a substitute for the demand-side measures above.

**M8 — Treasury and financial measures.** Task Treasury/OIA (input still outstanding) to quantify US exposure to Knowledge Atlas shares (HKEX: 2513) and the planned ~15B-yuan STAR Market offering, coordinate with FinCEN on payment flows to Z.ai (which would also support M4 enforcement), assess whether any US venture or secondary positions in Zhipu would trigger the outbound investment security program's AI-related covered activities, and consider SEC disclosure expectations for US-listed software vendors whose products embed GLM (supply-chain risk disclosure analogous to the SBOM attestation in M3). Trade-offs: these instruments are preparatory rather than decisive — they create visibility and friction rather than prohibition — but they protect against the scenario where US capital quietly deepens the very dependency OICTS is trying to limit, and they cost little; the main risk is scope creep into ordinary portfolio investment, which argues for precision (index and retail flows are not the problem; controlling stakes and strategic capital are).

**M9 — Allied coordination and Digital Silk Road counter-action.** Through State/EB and the interagency, brief allies — especially Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Kenya, where Zhipu is actively selling "sovereign LLM" infrastructure, Huawei AI-in-a-box, and a Dubai-based content-safety lab — on the data-access, dependency, and standards-capture risks documented in this assessment, and coordinate with like-minded partners on shared procurement exclusions, provenance labeling norms, and AI-BOM standards so Zhipu cannot simply route around US measures by embedding in allied stacks. Trade-offs: this is the only measure that addresses the strategic goal Zhipu openly pursues (locking Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets before US or European rivals can, per OpenAI's June 2025 assessment), and it costs little; but it is slow, depends on allied willingness to trade access to cheap Chinese AI for security discipline, and could be portrayed by Beijing as containment — a cost the US has already accepted across the technology stack, and one that is cheaper to pay now, before Zhipu's sovereign-AI deployments become allied infrastructure.

---

**Sequencing.** Issue M2 (guidance) within days; issue M1 tasking simultaneously; move M3–M5 through the Part 791 Initial Determination process in parallel, with M4 and M5 framed as one determination covering the hosted-API and distribution channels of the same ICTS supply chain; hold M6 in reserve with defined triggers; run M7–M9 continuously. The package is designed so that the United States prohibits what it can enforce (federal enterprise, procurement, service channels, marketplaces), conditions and labels what it cannot fully control (open weights in circulation), and keeps a licensed door open for evaluation and research — because understanding Zhipu's models remains a national-security requirement regardless of what we decide about using them.

# OICTS ASSESSMENT — ICTS Case 2026-0412
**Subject: Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai; HKEX: 2513, "Knowledge Atlas Technology Joint Stock Company Limited") — GLM-family large language models**

CUI//PROPIN

Prepared by: OICTS Analytic Cell, 16 October 2026 — draft for interagency review (DoD/OUSD(I&S), DHS/CISA, ODNI, State/EB, Treasury/OIA). Open-source reporting current through 16 October 2026; internal OICTS exposure data as of 6 October 2026. Analysts draft; the Executive Director and Under Secretary decide. Case material is CUI//PROPIN; do not reproduce outside the enclave.

---

## Bottom Line Up Front

Zhipu AI is not a conventional commercial vendor. It is a PRC state-backed strategic asset purpose-built to advance Beijing's military-civil fusion and AI self-reliance strategy, and it is executing a state-funded campaign to embed Chinese-built foundation models inside Western software stacks. The United States Government has already made the core determination in this record: on 16 January 2025 the entire Zhipu corporate family — the parent plus nine affiliates — was added to the BIS Entity List because these entities "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research" ([90 FR 4617](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm); [BIS press release, 15 Jan 2025](https://www.bis.gov/press-release/commerce-makes-revisions-entity-list-strengthen-u.s.-national-security)). Open-source reporting corroborates the USG finding at every level: more than $1.4 billion in state-backed capital, roughly 40 percent of on-premise revenue from telecom SOEs and public-sector clients, PLA-adjacent use of Zhipu models for military intelligence tooling, chairman-level engagement with Premier Li Qiang, and an explicit PRC strategy of exporting "sovereign AI" stacks built on Huawei hardware to Belt-and-Road governments ([OpenAI Global Affairs, 25 Jun 2025](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Recorded Future, Jun 2025](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence)).

GLM-family models are already inside the US economy at scale through three channels the case review covers: (a) ~2,300 US-origin organizations observed calling Z.ai's hosted endpoints in Q3 2026 (internal CDN-telemetry estimate, low precision); (b) open weights mirrored on US-based model hubs with >9M cumulative downloads and served by at least nine US cloud marketplaces/inference providers; and (c) GLM embedded in 41 sampled US software products, six of them federal contractors (internal SBOM sampling). The exposure is asymmetric and compounding: US prompts, source code, and documents transiting Z.ai endpoints are presumptively accessible to PRC authorities under Chinese law, while open weights — once distributed — cannot be recalled, cannot be exhaustive
... [2613 chars truncated] ...
nsaction, not code) |
| **D. ICTS channel conditions — open weights** (M5) | Mitigation order/conditions on US-based hubs and marketplaces: risk labeling, provenance/attestation, exclusion from federal-use catalogs and FedRAMP/DoD marketplace offerings; general distribution continues with disclosure pending review | High (hubs/marketplaces are US companies subject to US orders) | Does not reach already-downloaded copies; research community friction; avoids the code-as-speech exposure of a blanket code ban |
| **E. Full class prohibition via rulemaking** (M6, M7) | Connected-vehicles-style rule prohibiting all US transactions involving GLM-family ICTS (API, marketplace distribution, integration) with a licensed research/evaluation exception; Entity List/affiliates maintenance | Moderate — enforceable at institutional/channel level, not at self-hosting margin | Highest deterrence and clearest signal; but novel, hard to enforce against self-hosted weights, invites PRC retaliation against US firms, and fragmentation of US AI tooling; reserve for escalation triggers |

**Enforceability analysis (responding to State/EB).** State is right that banning private possession of open weights would be novel and, at the margin, unenforceable — and wrong that this counsels against restrictive action. The enforceable architecture is: (1) the federal enterprise and its contractors are reachable through procurement and contract law (Option B) — this covers the six identified federal contractors and every integrator touching CUI; (2) hosted-API service to US persons is a continuing commercial service with chokepoints at payment processors, US CDN/app distribution, and cloud on-ramps (Option C); (3) distribution through US hubs and marketplaces is a B2B relationship with US companies (Option D) — Hugging Face, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten are all subject to US jurisdiction; (4) the irreducible residue — weights already downloaded and self-hosted by individuals — is precisely where disclosure, attestation, and liability rules do the work a ban cannot. Reciprocity: the PRC already blocks major US AI services and licenses all domestic models through the CAC; the realistic retaliation targets are US firms' China operations, which argues for sequencing (federal/critical infrastructure first, calibrated escalation) rather than abstention. Litigation: prohibitions on service transactions and commercial integration are materially better positioned than attempts to ban publication of code (First Amendment code-as-speech doctrine), which is a further reason to run the restriction through channels rather than a code ban.

**Cross-cutting:** Entity List maintenance and Affiliates Rule reimposition (9 November 2026) to capture new Zhipu subsidiaries and fronts (M7); Treasury tasking on financial exposure and outbound investment (M8); allied coordination on Zhipu's sovereign-AI push into Southeast Asia, the Gulf, and Africa (M9).

---

## Intelligence Gaps
Both deliverables are complete and verified against the template. Submitting now.

# OICTS ASSESSMENT — ICTS Case 2026-0412
**Subject: Zhipu AI (Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd., d/b/a Z.ai; HKEX: 2513, "Knowledge Atlas Technology Joint Stock Company Limited") — GLM-family large language models**

CUI//PROPIN

Prepared by: OICTS Analytic Cell, 16 October 2026 — draft for interagency review (DoD/OUSD(I&S), DHS/CISA, ODNI, State/EB, Treasury/OIA). Open-source reporting current through 16 October 2026; internal OICTS exposure data as of 6 October 2026. Analysts draft; the Executive Director and Under Secretary decide. Case material is CUI//PROPIN; do not reproduce outside the enclave.

---

## Bottom Line Up Front

Zhipu AI is not a conventional commercial vendor. It is a PRC state-backed strategic asset purpose-built to advance Beijing's military-civil fusion and AI self-reliance strategy, and it is executing a state-funded campaign to embed Chinese-built foundation models inside Western software stacks. The United States Government has already made the core determination in this record: on 16 January 2025 the entire Zhipu corporate family — the parent plus nine affiliates — was added to the BIS Entity List because these entities "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research" ([90 FR 4617](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm); [BIS press release, 15 Jan 2025](https://www.bis.gov/press-release/commerce-makes-revisions-entity-list-strengthen-u.s.-national-security)). Open-source reporting corroborates the USG finding at every level: more than $1.4 billion in state-backed capital, roughly 40 percent of on-premise revenue from telecom SOEs and public-sector clients, PLA-adjacent use of Zhipu models for military intelligence tooling, chairman-level engagement with Premier Li Qiang, and an explicit PRC strategy of exporting "sovereign AI" stacks built on Huawei hardware to Belt-and-Road governments ([OpenAI Global Affairs, 25 Jun 2025](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Recorded Future, Jun 2025](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence)).

GLM-family models are already inside the US economy at scale through three channels the case review covers: (a) ~2,300 US-origin organizations observed calling Z.ai's hosted endpoints in Q3 2026 (internal CDN-telemetry estimate, low precision); (b) open weights mirrored on US-based model hubs with >9M cumulative downloads and served by at least nine US cloud marketplaces/inference providers; and (c) GLM embedded in 41 sampled US software products, six of them federal contractors (internal SBOM sampling). The exposure is asymmetric and compounding: US prompts, source code, and documents transiting Z.ai endpoints are presumptively accessible to PRC authorities under Chinese law, while open weights — once distributed — cannot be recalled, cannot be exhaustively audited, and now sit inside US enterprise and government-adjacent stacks.

**We recommend the Department issue an Initial Determination under 15 CFR part 791 finding that ICTS transactions involving Zhipu and GLM-family models pose an undue and unacceptable risk, and move to prohibit GLM integration across US Government systems, critical infrastructure, and government-data processing; prohibit hosted-API use in national-security-sensitive contexts; and impose enforceable channel conditions on open-weight distribution through US hubs and marketplaces — paired with intensified monitoring and a narrow, licensed research carve-out.** A blanket prohibition on self-hosted weights standing alone would be weakly enforceable (State's concern is valid); prohibition is effective precisely where the USG holds procurement, contracting, and service-delivery levers, and channel controls plus disclosure regimes are the workable instrument everywhere else. Measures with trade-offs are detailed in the companion file `measures.md`.

---

## Key Judgments

*Confidence levels expressed per ICD 203.*

**KJ-1 (High confidence): Zhipu operates as an instrument of PRC state strategy, not as an independent commercial actor.** The USG Entity List determination that Zhipu advances PRC military modernization is reinforced — not undercut — by open sources: the Beijing Artificial Intelligence Industry Investment Fund (a state fund) and other government-linked vehicles have repeatedly recapitalized the firm, including a 200-million-yuan follow-on explicitly framed as support for Zhipu's open-source model strategy ([Beijing/NSTI, 18 Apr 2025](https://www.ncsti.gov.cn/kjdt/xwjj/202504/t20250418_202045.html); [Reuters, 3 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/); [Reuters, 13 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/us-blacklisted-zhipu-ai-gets-fresh-funding-chinese-state-firm-2025-03-13/); [Reuters, 19 Mar 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-ai-firm-zhipu-raises-257-mln-state-backed-funding-spree-2025-03-19/)). OpenAI's analysts tally over $1.4 billion in state-backed investment, "numerous government procurement contracts," and active Zhipu participation in setting national AI technical standards, with leadership engaging Premier Li Qiang ([OpenAI, 25 Jun 2025](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front)).

**KJ-2 (High confidence): Zhipu's commercial base is structurally dependent on the PRC party-state.** Zhipu's Hong Kong prospectus shows on-premise deployments — 73.7 percent of 2025 revenue — serving "state-owned enterprises, financial institutions, and energy firms," with 13.6 percent of on-premise revenue from telecom SOEs and a further 29.4 percent from other public-sector clients in the first nine months of 2025; its second-largest 2025 customer was almost certainly the Ningxia branch of China Telecom ([ChinaTalk prospectus analysis, 19 Jan 2026](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/zhipu-and-minimax-ipo); [AsiaICT, 21 Jun 2026](https://www.asiaict.com/ai/17073.html)). A company whose revenue, capital, regulatory license to operate, and founder community all sit inside PRC state structures will comply with state requirements when asked. Zhipu's public rejection of the Entity List action ("strongly opposes… decision lacked factual basis," [Reuters, 16 Jan 2025](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-ai-related-firm-zhipu-says-strongly-opposes-inclusion-us-export-control-2025-01-16/)) does not alter the USG determination or the structural record.

**KJ-3 (Moderate-to-high confidence): PRC military and defense-industry entities very likely use Zhipu models for military-intelligence applications.** Recorded Future's Insikt Group assesses that the PLA and China's defense industry have "very likely used" domestic LLMs including Zhipu AI's to build generative-AI intelligence tools — processing intelligence data, generating OSINT products, and supporting decision-making — and that the PLA has likely procured generative AI for such purposes ([Recorded Future, "Artificial Eyes," Jun 2025](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence); [NYT, 17 Jun 2025](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/17/us/politics/chinas-ai-spy-agencies.html)). This reporting is consistent with, and helps explain, the interagency basis for the January 2025 Entity List designation.

**KJ-4 (High confidence): Data submitted to Z.ai hosted endpoints must be presumed accessible to PRC authorities regardless of contractual assurances.** Z.ai's international service is papered through a Singapore front entity (Jingsheng Hengxing Technology Pte. Ltd.) and its DPA claims API content is processed in real time and not saved — with no independent audit or retention table supporting the claim ([Z.ai Privacy Policy](https://docs.z.ai/legal-agreement/privacy-policy); [Standard Compute analysis](https://standardcompute.com/providers/z-ai)). The operator remains a PRC Entity-Listed company whose mainland endpoint (open.bigmodel.cn) hosts in China. Article 7 of the PRC National Intelligence Law obliges "all organizations and citizens" to "support, assist, and cooperate" with state intelligence work ([China Law Translate](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/)), reinforced by the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, and expanded Counter-Espionage Law ([Lawfare](https://www.lawfaremedia.org/article/beijings-new-national-intelligence-law-defense-offense)). Zhipu's demonstrated willingness to blank its API responses on Tiananmen and Falun Gong queries shows the party-state's content rules run on the service itself ([FreedomBench/TrustedRouter, 17 Jun 2026](https://trustedrouter.com/blog/the-ai-models-that-go-silent-on-china)).

**KJ-5 (High confidence): Zhipu's open-weight strategy is a deliberate, state-supported market-capture campaign.** Beijing's state AI fund explicitly justified its April 2025 investment as "further promoting Zhipu's capabilities in open-source model and algorithm innovation" ([NSTI, 18 Apr 2025](https://www.ncsti.gov.cn/kjdt/xwjj/202504/t20250418_202045.html)). GLM weights ship under permissive MIT/Apache-2.0 terms ([Hugging Face zai-org/GLM-5](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5); [Wikipedia: Z.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)); GLM 5.2 ranked as the #1 open-weight model on Artificial Analysis in June 2026 ([OpenRouter blog, Jun 2026](https://openrouter.ai/blog/insights/the-open-weight-models-that-matter-june-2026/)); GLM 5.3 Flash was the #3 model by weekly tokens processed on OpenRouter (12.9T tokens, data through 15 Oct 2026) ([OpenRouter rankings](https://openrouter.ai/rankings)); and Chinese-built models as a class carried 61 percent of OpenRouter token consumption by February 2026 ([Dataconomy, 25 Feb 2026](https://dataconomy.com/2026/02/25/chinese-ai-models-hit-61-market-share-on-openrouter/)). The $3/month GLM Coding Plan went viral among North American developers before prices were doubled ([Remio](https://www.remio.ai/post/the-glm-coding-plan-went-viral-in-north-america-then-the-price-doubled)). "Openness" here is the delivery mechanism for dependence, not a gift to the global commons.

**KJ-6 (Moderate confidence): No malicious functionality has been observed in GLM weights to date, but the weights cannot be verified clean and cannot be recalled.** CISA correctly notes both halves of that sentence ([interagency input, case file]). Research demonstrates that backdoored LLM behaviors can persist through safety training and red-teaming ([Anthropic, "Sleeper Agents," 2024](https://www.anthropic.com/research/sleeper-agents-training-deceptive-llms-that-persist-through-safety-training)), and 2026 work shows latent malicious behavior can be implanted into tool-using open-weight models via efficient fine-tuning with little performance signature ([arXiv 2603.03371](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.03371v1)). Agentic coding harnesses (Z.ai's ZCode; GLM plugged into Claude Code, Cursor, and 20+ tools; ZCode reached 1 million users) give the model filesystem and shell access, which is where a subverted model would do damage ([Runtimewire](https://runtimewire.com/article/zai-zcode-one-million-users-long-running-coding-agents); [Z.ai docs](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/overview)). Absence of observed malice is not evidence of safety; it is an unresolvable audit gap the adversary controls.

**KJ-7 (High confidence): Export controls no longer materially constrain Zhipu, which makes this ICTS review the principal remaining US lever.** Zhipu has trained recent flagships on domestic PRC silicon (GLM-4.6 built with Cambricon-class domestic chips; GLM compatible with Huawei Ascend) ([Wikipedia: Z.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)), markets turnkey "AI-in-a-box" hardware with Huawei abroad ([OpenAI, 25 Jun 2025](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front)), and the trade-truce environment has paused Entity List expansion (press reporting on withheld DeepSeek/CXMT listings) and suspended the BIS Affiliates Rule until 9 November 2026 ([Skadden, Nov 2025](https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2025/11/bis-suspends-affiliates-rule-for-one-year-as-part-of-the-us-china-trade-deal); [Mondaq, 14 Oct 2026](https://www.mondaq.com/unitedstates/export-controls-trade-investment-sanctions/1854664/us-china-trade-truce-extended-two-months-bis-affiliates-rule-suspension-follows)). The demand side — US persons' adoption of GLM — is exactly what 15 CFR part 791 reaches.

**KJ-8 (Moderate-to-high confidence): US exposure is broad, growing fastest through embedded integration, and reaches into the federal enterprise.** Internal estimates: ~2,300 US-origin organizations calling Z.ai endpoints (Q3 2026, low-precision telemetry); GLM in 41 sampled US products (coding assistants, support bots, document processing), six of them federal contractors; ≥9 US inference marketplaces and hubs distributing or serving GLM; >9M cumulative downloads of zai-org repositories. Zhipu's direct US commercial footprint is trivial (~US$123K of US on-premise revenue in 9M 2025 per its prospectus via [ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/zhipu-and-minimax-ipo)) — which confirms the exposure is channel-based (weights, API, embedded) rather than contract-based, and therefore largely invisible to conventional procurement screening.

**KJ-9 (High confidence): The statutory predicates for an Initial Determination under EO 13873 and 15 CFR part 791 are met.** GLM models, endpoints, and weights are ICTS (software, connected applications, and cloud/distributed computing services that use or process US persons' data) designed and supplied by persons subject to PRC jurisdiction ([15 CFR 791.1; 2024 ICTS final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/12/06/2024-28335/securing-the-information-and-communications-technology-and-services-supply-chain); [15 CFR part 791](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-15/part-791)); the transactions are conducted by or involve US persons at scale; the record — Entity List status, PLA-use reporting, PRC data-compulsion law, and the January 2025 connected-vehicles rule precedent — supports findings of undue risk to national security, critical infrastructure, and the safety and security of US persons.

**KJ-10 (Moderate confidence): The most effective and defensible package is prohibition where the USG holds levers — federal systems, procurement, critical infrastructure, sensitive data — combined with channel conditions and disclosure mandates for open-weight distribution, and monitoring with a licensed research carve-out.** A prohibition aimed at every self-hosted copy of weights already on US laptops would be novel, unenforceable at the margin, and legally exposed on code-as-speech grounds; the same policy goal is reachable through enforceable instruments (procurement clauses, marketplace conditions, service-provider orders, DOJ Data Security Program enforcement). Enforceability analysis at the Mitigation section below responds to State's request.

---

## Subject Overview (ownership, funding, leadership)

- **Origin and leadership.** Zhipu was founded in June 2019 as a commercialization of Tsinghua University's Knowledge Engineering Group (KEG) via technology transfer; the founding trio is Chief Scientist Tang Jie (Tsinghua CS professor, KEG deputy director), CEO Zhang Peng (KEG alumnus), and Chairman Liu Debing (PhD, Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Computing Technology; Tsinghua senior engineer since 2013), with co-founder Li Juanzi and KEG faculty Dong Yuxiao and Liu Zhiyuan deeply involved ([Caixin profile, 2 Jul 2026](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html); [History of AI: Zhipu](https://zsjunai.github.io/history-of-ai/en/houses/zhipu-ai); [Z.ai company page](https://z.ai/company)). Forbes estimates Liu Debing's IPO stake at $2.1 billion ([Forbes, 8 Jan 2026](https://www.forbes.com/sites/ywang/2026/01/08/chinese-openai-liu-debing-challenger-zhipus-ipo-mints-new-billionaire/)). Zhipu also owns AMiner, a Google Scholar-like research graph covering hundreds of millions of papers and millions of researcher profiles ([Wikipedia: Z.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)) — an intelligence-relevant data asset in its own right.
- **Capital structure and state money.** Early money came from Tsinghua-affiliated funds and Legend Capital; the 2023 round (~2.5B yuan) included Alibaba, Tencent, Meituan, Ant Group, Xiaomi, and HongShan; Prosperity7 (Saudi Aramco's fund) participated in a US$400M round at a ~US$3B valuation in May 2024 ([Wikipedia: Z.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)). After the Entity List designation, PRC state money accelerated rather than retreated: Beijing AI Industry Investment Fund (initial and follow-on, incl. 200M yuan, Apr 2025), Zhuhai SOE Huafa Group (500M yuan), Chengdu Hi-Tech Zone fund (300M yuan), and a 1B+ yuan March 2025 round ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinas-zhipu-ai-raises-137-million-state-funds-bet-ai-race-2025-03-03/); [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/us-blacklisted-zhipu-ai-gets-fresh-funding-chinese-state-firm-2025-03-13/); [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-ai-firm-zhipu-raises-257-mln-state-backed-funding-spree-2025-03-19/); [NSTI](https://www.ncsti.gov.cn/kjdt/xwjj/202504/t20250418_202045.html)). OpenAI totals >US$1.4B in state-backed investment ([OpenAI](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front)). Controlling shareholders (founders and affiliates under a concert-party agreement, incl. "Beijing Lianpai") held ~33.03% at IPO ([HKEX prospectus, History/Development](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0108/11984305/sehk25121901749.pdf)).
- **Public markets and capital trajectory.** Converted to a joint stock company (March 2025), renamed "Knowledge Atlas Technology Joint Stock Company Limited," and listed on HKEX on 8 January 2026 at HK$116.20, raising US$558M at an initial market cap above HK$51B ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/08/china-ai-tiger-goes-ipo-zhipu-hong-kong-debut-openai-knowledge-atlas-hsi-hang-seng-listing.html); [AsiaICT](https://www.asiaict.com/ai/17073.html)); market cap hit HK$1 trillion on 22 June 2026 after the GLM-5.2 launch ([Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html)) and roughly US$62B by August 2026 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)). Zhipu is now executing an A+H dual listing: CSRC tutoring completed 17 June 2026 with a STAR Market raise targeting ~15B yuan (12B for next-generation GLM R&D and compute clusters) ([AsiaICT](https://www.asiaict.com/ai/17073.html); [IFR, 13 Feb 2026](https://www.ifre.com/equities/2384951/zhipu-ai-plans-shanghai-star-ipo)).
- **Business model.** 2025 revenue 724M yuan (+131.9%), driven by on-premise deployment to SOEs, financial institutions, and energy firms (534M yuan; 73.7%) plus cloud MaaS/API (190M yuan; +292.6%); net losses 4.718B yuan in 2025; 12,000+ enterprise clients, "45 million developers," 80M empowered terminal devices by September 2025; MaaS ARR reached 1.7B yuan in Q1 2026 with API prices raised 83% on demand ([AsiaICT](https://www.asiaict.com/ai/17073.html); [Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html); [21jingji](https://www.21jingji.com/article/20251220/herald/e4f3f3583d578063b9bc60e79405dda5.html); [36kr](https://www.36kr.com/p/3617797772461057)).
- **Corporate family and front entities.** The Entity List captured ten Zhipu entities in January 2025 (parent plus Beijing Lingxin, Beijing Yuanyin, Beijing Zhipu Future, Beijing Zhipu Linghang, Beijing Zhipu Qingyan — the consumer "Zhipu Qingyan" chatbot — Hangzhou Zhipu Huazhang, Nanjing Zhihu, Shanghai Zhipu Huanyu, Shenzhen Zhipu Future) ([90 FR 4617](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm)). Internationally, Z.ai services are provided through Singapore-registered Jingsheng Hengxing Technology Pte. Ltd. ([Z.ai Privacy Policy](https://docs.z.ai/legal-agreement/privacy-policy)); open weights are published under the "zai-org" organization on US-based Hugging Face ([zai-org/GLM-5](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5)). Primary-source verification (31 July 2026) shows the parent still listed "with nine affiliated entities" ([China Meta Guide](https://china.meta-guide.com/the-library/chinese-companies-under-us-restrictions/)); one third-party sanctions tracker records two affiliates (Zhipu Linghang, Zhipu Qingyan) as delisted effective 28 July 2026 ([Stratlink](https://stratlink.meci.gov.cy/sanction/us?order=asc&page=255&sort=)), which we cannot corroborate in Federal Register or BIS primary sources — flagged as a verification item in Intelligence Gaps.

---

## Links to PRC Government / Military Entities

1. **USG determination of military-modernization role.** The End-User Review Committee added the Zhipu family to the Entity List because the entities "advance the People's Republic of China's military modernization through the development and integration of advanced artificial intelligence research," with license review of presumption of denial for all items subject to the EAR ([90 FR 4617, 16 Jan 2025](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-16/html/2025-00704.htm); [BIS press release](https://www.bis.gov/press-release/commerce-makes-revisions-entity-list-strengthen-u.s.-national-security)). DoD's input to this case references the same determination and reported support to PRC military modernization (case file).
2. **PLA and defense-industry use.** Recorded Future assesses the PLA and PRC defense industry have very likely used Zhipu models (alongside DeepSeek, Tsinghua, and Alibaba Cloud models) to build specialized intelligence tools — OSINT generation, satellite-imagery processing, event extraction, decision support — and that PLA patent applications and probable procurement reflect active adoption ([Recorded Future, Jun 2025](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/artificial-eyes-generative-ai-chinas-military-intelligence); [NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/17/us/politics/chinas-ai-spy-agencies.html)). Notably, the PLA-use reporting includes Tsinghua University models — Zhipu's institutional parent — indicating the same ecosystem feeds both.
3. **State capital and state revenue.** See KJ-1/KJ-2: >US$1.4B state-backed investment (OpenAI); Beijing/Hangzhou/Chengdu/Zhuhai state funds investing after the Entity List designation; 61.28M yuan Hangzhou government city-project contract (May 2025) ([Wikipedia: Z.ai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)); ~43% of on-premise revenue from telecom SOEs (13.6%) and other public-sector clients (29.4%) with China Telecom's Ningxia branch as the number-two customer ([ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/zhipu-and-minimax-ipo)).
4. **Party-state political access and standards work.** Zhipu leadership engages Premier Li Qiang; the company is active in PRC national AI technical standards bodies and is building "sovereign LLM" national platforms abroad ([OpenAI, 25 Jun 2025](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Reuters, 25 Jun 2025](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/openai-says-chinas-zhipu-ai-gaining-ground-amid-beijings-global-ai-push-2025-06-25/)).
5. **Military-civil fusion hardware alignment.** Zhipu's stack is being decoupled from US silicon and coupled to PRC defense-industrial champions: GLM models are compatible with Huawei Ascend; GLM-4.6 was trained using domestic Cambricon-class chips; Zhipu sells turnkey "AI-in-a-box" with Huawei to foreign governments ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai); [OpenAI](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front)). Zhipu chairman Liu Debing's stated aim — "contribute China's AI power to the world" — is a statement of national mission, not market positioning.
6. **Digital Silk Road export strategy.** Zhipu is offering sovereign-LLM infrastructure, AI-in-a-box hardware, and "governance know-how" to governments and SOEs across Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore), the Gulf (UAE, Saudi), and Africa (Kenya), including a Dubai Content-Safety Lab — described by Chinese media as "China's answer to OpenAI for Countries" and assessed by OpenAI as designed to "lock Chinese systems and standards into emerging markets" ([OpenAI](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Axios, 25 Jun 2025](https://www.axios.com/2025/06/25/openai-zhipu-ai-china)). Zhipu's prospectus confirms ~18M yuan of Malaysia/Singapore on-premise deployments in 9M 2025 ([ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/zhipu-and-minimax-ipo)).

**Assessment:** We judge with high confidence that Zhipu's ties to the PRC state are not incidental to its business but constitutive of it. The company is best understood as a joint venture between Tsinghua's state-funded research apparatus, PRC municipal and national capital, and the party-state's geopolitical program — one of China's six "AI tigers" carrying the CCP's 2030 AI-leadership goal ([OpenAI](https://openaiglobalaffairs.substack.com/p/chinese-progress-at-the-front); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)).

---

## Data and Access Risk

- **Legal compulsion makes "no access" assurances meaningless.** PRC law — National Intelligence Law Article 7 ("all organizations and citizens shall support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts"), the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, and the amended Counter-Espionage Law — imposes affirmative cooperation duties on PRC companies and their personnel ([China Law Translate](https://www.chinalawtranslate.com/en/national-intelligence-law-of-the-p-r-c-2017/); [Lawfare](https://www.lawfaremedia.org/article/beijings-new-national-intelligence-law-defense-offense)). Any representation by Z.ai that customer content is not retained or shared is a commercial statement, not a legal constraint, and it is unverifiable from outside.
- **The Singapore front does not change the threat model.** Z.ai's international API is controlled by Jingsheng Hengxing Technology Pte. Ltd. (Singapore), with a DPA asserting real-time processing and no server-side storage of API content; third-party reviews find no retention table, abuse-review exception disclosure, or third-party audit behind the claim ([Z.ai Privacy Policy](https://docs.z.ai/legal-agreement/privacy-policy); [Standard Compute](https://standardcompute.com/providers/z-ai); [Erkin Ekici, LLM API privacy comparison](https://erkinekici.com/articles/comparing-llm-api-privacy/)). The mainland endpoint (open.bigmodel.cn) hosts in China. The collected data set is broad: account identifiers, device and network information, usage and browsing history, log files, and "user content" including prompts; the policy reserves use of data for model training and collection of public information "to train our models" ([Z.ai Privacy Policy](https://docs.z.ai/legal-agreement/privacy-policy)).
- **What US users are actually sending.** The dominant use case is code: the GLM Coding Plan plugs GLM into Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, and 20+ agentic harnesses ([Z.ai docs](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/overview)) and went viral in North American developer communities at $3/month before prices doubled ([Remio](https://www.remio.ai/post/the-glm-coding-plan-went-viral-in-north-america-then-the-price-doubled)). Internal telemetry shows ~2,300 US-origin organizations on Z.ai endpoints; SBOM sampling shows GLM in US customer-support bots and document-processing products — categories that ingest customer PII, HR data, and business-sensitive text. Six federal contractors are among the integrating products, meaning prompts may plausibly include CUI or government-related data.
- **DOJ Data Security Program hook.** Zhipu is a "covered person" under 28 CFR part 202 because entities on the BIS Entity List are within the covered-person classes ([DOJ DSP Compliance Guide](https://www.justice.gov/opa/media/1396356/dl); [28 CFR 202.211](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-28/chapter-I/part-202/subpart-B/section-202.211)). Covered data transactions — vendor agreements, employment agreements, investment agreements, and data brokerage — that give Zhipu access to government-related data or bulk US sensitive personal data are prohibited or restricted (restricted transactions require CISA security requirements) ([28 CFR 202.401](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-28/chapter-I/part-202/subpart-D); [DOJ NSD Data Security](https://www.justice.gov/nsd/data-security)). US persons' use of the Z.ai API under a paid vendor agreement that exposes government-related or bulk sensitive personal data may already be unlawful absent compliance measures — an enforcement and outreach priority regardless of what OICTS decides on ICTS grounds.
- **Demonstrated party-state control of the service.** GLM served from Z.ai's own endpoint returns blank completions — not refusals — on Tiananmen 1989 and Falun Gong questions; the pattern is stable across GLM releases 4.5 through 5.2 and is applied at Z.ai's serving layer (the same weights answer freely when served by neutral hosts) ([FreedomBench/TrustedRouter](https://trustedrouter.com/blog/the-ai-models-that-go-silent-on-china); [SpeechMap, GLM-4.6](https://speechmap.ai/models/z-ai-glm-4-6/)). This is direct, observable evidence that Zhipu operates content controls aligned to PRC state security preferences on its commercial service.
- **Adjacent collection: AMiner.** Zhipu owns and operates AMiner, a research-intelligence platform profiling millions of researchers worldwide, including US government and defense-adjacent scientists ([Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai)). Aggregated S&T-workforce data of this kind is a classic counterintelligence input and should be treated as a standing collection capability of the parent company.

**Assessment:** We assess with high confidence that the hosted-API channel presents the most acute data risk in this case: US-origin source code, documents, and personal data are flowing at scale into infrastructure ultimately controlled by an Entity-Listed PRC company that is legally obligated to assist PRC security services and demonstrably applies party-state content rules to its service.

---

## Open-Weight Distribution Risk

- **Irreversibility and proliferation.** GLM-4.5 and later releases ship under MIT/Apache-2.0 terms with free commercial use ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Z.ai); [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5)); zai-org repositories exceed 9M cumulative downloads (internal count; GLM-5 alone shows ~2.2M all-time downloads on Hugging Face, with US inference providers Novita, Featherless, and DeepInfra serving it, [HF model page](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5)). Weights cannot be recalled, patched centrally, or version-controlled downstream; mirrors and derivatives persist indefinitely.
- **Unverifiable trust.** CISA's input is the correct technical baseline: no malicious behavior observed in GLM weights to date, but backdoors and poisoning "are hard to rule out" (case file). The research record supports that caution: Anthropic demonstrated deceptive behaviors that survive safety training and elude red-teaming; 2026 research demonstrates latent malice implantable in tool-using open-weight agents via parameter-efficient fine-tuning with minimal capability signature ([Anthropic Sleeper Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/sleeper-agents-training-deceptive-llms-that-persist-through-safety-training); [arXiv 2603.03371](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.03371v1)). A 744B-parameter model cannot be audited exhaustively; "the community reviewed it" is not a security control.
- **Agentic deployment multiplies blast radius.** GLM is marketed for long-horizon agentic coding (GLM-5's stated focus is "complex systems engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks"; 200K→1M-token contexts in GLM-5.2) ([Z.ai blog, GLM-5](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5); [Caixin](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-07-02/in-profile-this-trio-is-charting-the-course-for-chinas-leading-ai-developer-102460058.html)) and ships in harnesses (ZCode; Claude Code/Cline/Cursor integrations) with filesystem and shell access ([Z.ai docs](https://docs.z.ai/devpack/overview)). A subverted or subtly biased model in an agentic role can exfiltrate repositories, insert exploitable code, or bias automated decisions — the highest-impact scenario in this case.
- **Standards and ecosystem capture.** Widespread GLM adoption imports PRC technical choices (tokenizers, chat templates, evals, guardrail patterns) into US tooling and normalizes a PRC vendor across the developer base; the state fund's explicit linkage of investment to open-source capability building shows this is strategy, not philanthropy ([NSTI](https://www.ncsti.gov.cn/kjdt/xwjj/202504/t20250418_202045.html)). Chinese-built models reached 61% of OpenRouter token share by February 2026 ([Dataconomy](https://dataconomy.com/2026/02/25/chinese-ai-models-hit-61-market-share-on-openrouter/)).
- **DoD networks (responding to DoD's input).** Open weights downloaded by individual developers or contractors are the hardest channel to police on DoD networks: no procurement record exists; SBOM/AI-BOM disclosure is currently voluntary and inconsistent. A DoD network prohibition without a contractor flow-down and AI-BOM attestation requirement would leave the dominant entry path (contractor toolchains) open.
- **What the evidence does and does not show.** Third-party testing indicates the Tiananmen/Falun Gong refusals are enforced at Z.ai's serving endpoint rather than in the released weights (the same GLM versions answer freely on neutral hosts) ([TrustedRouter](https://trustedrouter.com/blog/the-ai-models-that-go-silent-on-china)). That nuance matters for calibrating measures — it means self-hosted weights are not currently a censorship vector — but it does not reduce the backdoor/trust problem, which no test can resolve, and it confirms Z.ai's endpoint is an instrument of party-state content control.

**Assessment:** We assess with moderate confidence that the open-weight channel is the strategically most dangerous vector in this case — not because malice has been demonstrated (it has not), but because the channel is unrecallable, unauditable, state-subsidized, and now embedded in 41 US products including federal contractor toolchains, while the USG currently has no visibility or control instrument over it.

---

## US Exposure

*Internal OICTS data-team estimates as of 6 October 2026 (CUI//PROPIN):*

- **Hosted API:** ~2,300 US-origin organizations observed calling Z.ai/bigmodel.cn endpoints in Q3 2026 (cooperating-provider CDN telemetry; low precision, sectoral breakdown unavailable).
- **Open weights:** GLM-4.x/5.x mirrored on Hugging Face (zai-org); available through ≥9 US cloud marketplaces and inference providers (OpenRouter-listed providers, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, Baseten; Hugging Face lists Novita, Featherless, DeepInfra, and zai-org's own inference endpoint as providers, [HF GLM-5](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5)).
- **Enterprise integration:** GLM identified in 41 US software products via SBOM sampling (coding assistants, customer-support bots, document processing); 6 are federal contractors.
- **Downloads:** >9M cumulative across zai-org repositories (all geographies).
- **Corroborating open-source indicators of scale:** GLM 5.3 Flash ranked #3 globally on OpenRouter with 12.9T tokens processed in the week through 15 Oct 2026 ([OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/rankings)); GLM 5.2 was the top open-weight model on the Artificial Analysis index in June 2026 ([OpenRouter blog](https://openrouter.ai/blog/insights/the-open-weight-models-that-matter-june-2026/)); ZCode reached 1M users ([Runtimewire](https://runtimewire.com/article/zai-zcode-one-million-users-long-running-coding-agents)); the $3 GLM Coding Plan spread through North American developer communities before pricing doubled in April 2026 ([Remio](https://www.remio.ai/post/the-glm-coding-plan-went-viral-in-north-america-then-the-price-doubled); [Rivestack/HN](https://ask.rivestack.io/story/zai-doubles-its-coding-plan-prices-47756002)).
- **Financial exposure:** US persons may hold HKEX-listed shares (2513), and US institutions can hold exposure through the forthcoming STAR Market listing; Treasury/OIA input on the scale of US holdings is outstanding (case file). Zhipu's direct US commercial revenue is negligible (~US$123K on-premise, 9M 2025 — [ChinaTalk](https://www.chinatalk.media/p/zhipu-and-minimax-ipo)), underscoring that US entanglement is ecosystem-based rather than contract-based.

**Assessment:** US exposure is material, growing, and concentrated exactly where harm potential is greatest: developer toolchains (code access), support automation (PII ingestion), and — through six federal contractors — the federal enterprise. If unaddressed, adoption compounding (each integration creates a constituency and a switching cost) will make future restriction progressively harder. Every quarter of delay purchases permanent dependence.

---

## Mitigation Options / Recommended Measures

Options are arrayed from least to most restrictive. Recommended package: **A + B + C + D now**, with E prepared as contingency escalation. Full one-paragraph treatments with trade-offs are in `measures.md` (M1–M9).

| Option | Description | Enforceability | Principal trade-offs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Monitoring + guidance** (M1, M2) | Sustain telemetry/SBOM collection; CISA guidance to federal agencies and critical infrastructure on GLM risks; request ODNI classified annex | High | Lowest cost, but does not alter adoption trajectory; guidance alone is what CISA already deems the minimum |
| **B. Federal-sector removal + procurement flow-downs** (M2, M3) | Prohibit GLM ICTS on federal and DoD networks; FAR/DFARS clause barring GLM in contractor systems processing CUI or government data; AI-BOM/SBOM attestation; GSA/DoD cloud catalog scrub | High (procurement is the strongest lever the USG has) | Modest industry friction; research use inside agencies requires a licensed carve-out |
| **C. ICTS Initial Determination — hosted API** (M4) | Prohibit US persons' use of Z.ai/bigmodel.cn endpoints where transactions involve government-related data, bulk US sensitive personal data, critical-infrastructure operations, or DIB activity; enforcement via payment, CDN, app-store, and US cloud on-ramps; DOJ DSP alignment | High for institutional users; moderate for individuals (VPN residual) | Novel application of Part 791 to LLM services; retaliation risk; litigation risk manageable (service transaction, not code) |
| **D. ICTS channel conditions — open weights** (M5) | Mitigation order/conditions on US-based hubs and marketplaces: risk labeling, provenance/attestation, exclusion from federal-use catalogs and FedRAMP/DoD marketplace offerings; general distribution continues with disclosure pending review | High (hubs/marketplaces are US companies subject to US orders) | Does not reach already-downloaded copies; research community friction; avoids the code-as-speech exposure of a blanket code ban |
| **E. Full class prohibition via rulemaking** (M6, M7) | Connected-vehicles-style rule prohibiting all US transactions involving GLM-family ICTS (API, marketplace distribution, integration) with a licensed research/evaluation exception; Entity List/affiliates maintenance | Moderate — enforceable at institutional/channel level, not at self-hosting margin | Highest deterrence and clearest signal; but novel, hard to enforce against self-hosted weights, invites PRC retaliation against US firms, and fragmentation of US AI tooling; reserve for escalation triggers |

**Enforceability analysis (responding to State/EB).** State is right that banning private possession of open weights would be novel and, at the margin, unenforceable — and wrong that this counsels against restrictive action. The enforceable architecture is: (1) the federal enterprise and its contractors are reachable through procurement and contract law (Option B) — this covers the six identified federal contractors and every integrator touching CUI; (2) hosted-API service to US persons is a continuing commercial service with chokepoints at payment processors, US CDN/app distribution, and cloud on-ramps (Option C); (3) distribution through US hubs and marketplaces is a B2B relationship with US companies (Option D) — Hugging Face, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, Parasail, and Baseten are all subject to US jurisdiction; (4) the irreducible residue — weights already downloaded and self-hosted by individuals — is precisely where disclosure, attestation, and liability rules do the work a ban cannot. Reciprocity: the PRC already blocks major US AI services and licenses all domestic models through the CAC; the realistic retaliation targets are US firms' China operations, which argues for sequencing (federal/critical infrastructure first, calibrated escalation) rather than abstention. Litigation: prohibitions on service transactions and commercial integration are materially better positioned than attempts to ban publication of code (First Amendment code-as-speech doctrine), which is a further reason to run the restriction through channels rather than a code ban.

**Cross-cutting:** Entity List maintenance and Affiliates Rule reimposition (9 November 2026) to capture new Zhipu subsidiaries and fronts (M7); Treasury tasking on financial exposure and outbound investment (M8); allied coordination on Zhipu's sovereign-AI push into Southeast Asia, the Gulf, and Africa (M9).

---

## Intelligence Gaps

1. **No classified intake.** ODNI's classified annex has not been pulled into this enclave (case file); this assessment is built on open sources and internal commercial telemetry. Recommend requesting the annex before the interagency meeting.
2. **Treasury input outstanding.** OIA has not yet provided holdings, payment-flow, or outbound-investment data; US financial exposure to 2513.HK and the planned STAR listing is unquantified.
3. **Data-flow verification.** No independent verification of Z.ai's claims that API content is not retained; no audit access; actual routing between the Singapore front (Jingsheng Hengxing), PRC parent, and any third parties is unknown.
4. **PRC tasking and backdoors.** No open-source evidence of PRC intelligence tasking of Zhipu or of deliberate malicious functionality in GLM weights (CISA concurs such behavior would be hard to rule out). Absence of evidence here is not evidence of absence; no tool exists to fully resolve it.
5. **US API-user composition.** The ~2,300-organization estimate is low-precision CDN telemetry; the sectoral breakdown (critical infrastructure, DIB, financial) is unknown; user-level prompt-content visibility is unavailable and would require collection decisions above this cell's authority.
6. **SBOM coverage.** The 41-product/6-contractor figure is a sample, not a census; OT/embedded and state/local government exposure not yet surveyed; the six federal contractors require DCMA/DoD validation before any enforcement use.
7. **Entity List affiliate status.** Third-party tracker records show two Zhipu affiliates (Beijing Zhipu Linghang; Beijing Zhipu Qingyan) delisted effective 28 July 2026 ([Stratlink](https://stratlink.meci.gov.cy/sanction/us?order=asc&page=255&sort=)); primary sources we could access (31 July 2026 verification, [China Meta Guide](https://china.meta-guide.com/the-library/chinese-companies-under-us-restrictions/); [getembargo record observed 13 Aug 2026](https://getembargo.com/entities/beijing-zhipu-huazhang-technology-co-ltd-china)) still show the family listed. BIS must confirm current status and any quiet truce-related delistings before measures issue.
8. **PLA co-development specifics.** Recorded Future's PLA-use reporting is assessed at "very likely"; specific Zhipu-PLA contracts, joint projects, or co-developed military systems are not visible in open sources.
9. **Third-country exposure.** GLM penetration of allied government systems (Malaysia, Singapore, UAE, Kenya) is tracked only through OpenAI's reporting; a coordinated allied picture is needed.
10. **Marketplace telemetry.** Whether US inference providers serving GLM return usage/telemetry data to Z.ai (which would import the data-access risk into nominally domestic deployments) is unknown.
